text: Chechnya's law enforcement and security officials launched an anti-gay purge in 2017, rounding up dozens of men on suspicion of being gay and holding them in unofficial detention facilities where they were humiliated, starved and tortured; Human Rights Watch says top-level local authorities sanctioned the purge. UN experts reported a new wave of arrests from December 2018, with two deaths allegedly caused by torture in detention.
short: Chechen security forces tortured men suspected of being gay in purges in 2017 and 2018-19 (HRW, UN)

source.name: Human Rights Watch: “They Have Long Arms and They Can Find Me” — Anti-Gay Purge by Local Authorities in Russia’s Chechen Republic
source.quote: They rounded up dozens of men on suspicion of being gay, held them in unofficial detention facilities for days, humiliated, starved, and tortured them.

additionalSources.name: UNRIC (United Nations): LGBT community in Chechnya faces ‘new wave of persecution’: UN human rights experts
additionalSources.quote: More than 40 people have reportedly been arrested since December 2018 because of their perceived sexual orientation: the two deaths allegedly occurred as a result of torture during detention.
